statement: No realignment/battery items were disclosed for 2023-H1..2024-H2; treated as 0 in adjusted EBIT.
rationale: FY2023 and FY2024 EBIT bridges (S003 p.55, S007 p.65) show no extraordinary bracket; H1 2024 deck mentions only a qualitative supply disruption.
sensitivity: If undisclosed one-offs existed in 2023/24, the 2023/24 adjusted baseline would be higher and the recovery weaker than shown.

statement: No additional US import tariffs before April 2025; treated as 0.
rationale: Section 232 auto tariffs took effect 3 April 2025 (Phase 1 research); Porsche first reports tariff costs in H1 2025.
sensitivity: Low: pre-2025 MFN duties are part of normal cost of sales.

statement: Impairments inside automotive D&A are 0 where not disclosed. Not applied to any period since the Oct 2026 source re-check: FY2023 (EUR 2m) and FY2024 (EUR 3m) automotive impairments were found in the segment reporting tables of S004 and S008, so H2 2023 and H2 2024 are DERIVED as FY - H1.
rationale: Kept as a fallback rule for any period without a disclosed figure; currently every period in the window has a disclosed or derived value.
sensitivity: None at present. Before the re-check, 0 was used for 2023-H2 and 2024-H2; the disclosed values (2 and 3) lower clean D&A in those halves by EUR 2m and 3m.

statement: H1 2026 impairments of EUR 61m (eBike 43 + Cellforce 18) are inside automotive D&A.
rationale: Both are published impairments of automotive subsidiaries; their line item is not confirmed (Inputs M-row note).
sensitivity: Alternative 0: clean D&A +61m, L3 -61m in H1 2026; shown as a sensitivity column.

statement: FY2026 automotive revenue = group revenue guidance x H1 2026 automotive share of group revenue (88.0%).
rationale: Porsche guides automotive margins but not automotive revenue.
sensitivity: The share fell steadily from 92.5% (2023-H1) to 88.0% (2026-H1) as Financial Services grew. Tested: +/-1pp share moves the implied H2 2026 automotive EBITDA margin by only ~0.05pp (13.83%-13.92% at mid guidance).

statement: The FY2026 extraordinary-expense figure of EUR 0.8-0.9bn (stated by the CFO on the H1 2026 earnings call, S027 transcript; not an amount in Porsche written guidance) is on the same net basis as the H1 2026 figure (EUR ~0.1bn).
rationale: The EUR 0.8-0.9bn is transcript-derived: the CFO stated it on the H1 2026 call (S027, Investing.com transcript, AI-assisted and editor-reviewed): net effect ~EUR 100m in H1, EUR 800-900m for the full year. Porsche written outlook (S016 slide 14) gives no amount and states that higher realignment expenses are expected to be offset by reversing provisions. Consistent with press release S018: realignment costs expected to reach a three-digit-million amount in H2 2026.
sensitivity: If the guidance were gross of provision releases, implied H2 exceptional charges would be lower.

statement: H2 2026 tariff expense = H1 2026 tariff expense (EUR 0.4bn). Analyst assumption; the CFO's call remark of ~EUR 0.7bn for FY2026 (S027) would imply ~EUR 0.3bn.
rationale: Analyst assumption. Porsche written guidance gives no tariff amount. On the H1 2026 call the CFO said guidance includes around EUR 700m of tariff impacts for FY2026 (S027, transcript), which would imply ~EUR 300m in H2 after H1 EUR 0.4bn.
sensitivity: Level L2 only; L0 and L1 do not depend on it. With EUR 300m instead of 400m the implied H2 2026 L2 margin is 11.00% instead of 11.54% at all midpoints (range 8.69%-13.38% instead of 9.23%-13.94%).

statement: Guidance ranges are combined as a grid of low / mid / high values, treated as independent.
rationale: Porsche gives ranges without saying which ends go together.
sensitivity: Extreme corners (low revenue with high margin) are included, so the range is wide on purpose.

statement: Derived H2 values inherit rounding of their inputs (one-offs EUR 0.1bn -> +/-EUR 100m on H2 one-offs).
applies_to: all views using H2 one-off values
rationale: H2 = FY - H1; both inputs rounded to EUR 0.1bn.
